project.name: messq
project.shortDescription: Single-binary, single-node queue daemon for Linux: at-least-once delivery, ack/nak/term/extend, ack timeout, bounded redelivery, DLQ, cursors, replay, and a durable per-message event journal (`messq trace`). SQLite/WAL storage, HTTP/JSON API, CLI-first ops.

labels.name: area:storage
labels.description: SQLite store, schema, durability, recovery, retention

labels.name: area:core
labels.description: Delivery state machine, consumers, lifecycle semantics

labels.name: area:api
labels.description: HTTP protocol surface and error model

labels.name: area:testing
labels.description: Harnesses: crash, property, fuzz, soak, goldens

labels.name: area:ops
labels.description: Operational features: retention, backup, doctor, bench

milestones.title: M1: Foundations
milestones.description: Repo bootstrap, CI quality gates, core primitives (ULID, subject matcher, Clock seam), and the normative semantics spec + ADRs — written before feature code.

milestones.title: M2: Durable store & publish
milestones.description: SQLite store with enforced pragmas, single-writer group commit, durability modes, streams + publish + dedup + peek, crash harness with three-valued ledger oracle, verify + recovery. Exit gate: SIGKILL loop loses zero acknowledged publishes; >=5k durable 1KiB msg/s on NVMe.

milestones.title: M3: Delivery engine
milestones.description: Consumers, cursors, claim, flow control, fenced ack/nak/term/extend, timeout sweeper with backoff, DLQ-as-stream, reference model + rapid property suite. Exit: poison message dead-letters after exactly max_deliver attempts; invariants green over 1e5 random ops including restart.

milestones.title: M4: API & daemon
milestones.description: Complete HTTP/JSON surface with stable error envelope, token auth + listener policy, daemon lifecycle (drain, SIGHUP, sd_notify, hardened systemd unit), contract + curl golden tests. Exit: systemctl restart mid-load loses nothing; the five-line shell worker is a passing CI test.

milestones.title: M5: Observability
milestones.description: Event vocabulary wired through the writer, slog JSON + human handlers with sampling policy, messq trace + events API, Prometheus metrics + shipped alerts and dashboard. Exit: trace renders a full timed-out/naked/acked timeline; golden log/metric tests green.

milestones.title: M6: CLI & client
milestones.description: Go client package (used by the CLI), cobra command tree with output contract, sub --exec worker mode, quickstart, completions, testscript golden suite. Exit: cold machine to first trace in under 60 seconds.

milestones.title: M7: Operations
milestones.description: Retention + housekeeping + disk safety, seek/replay with destructive-action discipline, guarded DLQ redrive, backup + doctor, bench with honest published numbers. Exit: a full incident is drivable from the CLI alone; a week-long stream does not grow unbounded.

milestones.title: M8: Hardening & v1.0
milestones.description: Fault-injection matrix (ENOSPC/EIO/clock/disconnect), fuzz corpus + soak, upgrade fixtures, packaging (deb/rpm/container), the 1.0 documentation set, release gates and the v1.0.0 tag.

milestones.title: M9: Phase 2
milestones.description: Demand-ordered post-1.0 features, each shipping with its own invariant, events, metrics and docs: delayed delivery, ordered-by-subject consumers, rate limiting, native TLS, worker attribution, audit export.

issues.title: Repo bootstrap: module, layout, Makefile, licence, CI skeleton
issues.summary: Create the repository skeleton: go.mod (Go 1.25+, pinned toolchain), the package layout from PLAN.md section 3.3 (cmd/messq, internal/{queue,store,api,obs,cli,model,testutil}, pkg/client, docs, packaging), Apache-2.0 LICENSE, DCO CONTRIBUTING.md, SECURITY.md stub, and a Makefile with build/test/race/lint/cover targets. Add a minimal GitHub Actions workflow that builds a CGO_ENABLED=0 static binary for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 and runs go vet. messq version must print version/commit/date injected via -ldflags. Acceptance: make ci is green on the empty skeleton; the produced binary is static (verified with ldd); repo is legally unambiguous to a first contributor.

issues.title: CI quality gates: lint config, race, coverage floors, govulncheck
issues.summary: Wire the quality gates that must exist from the first commit so discipline never has to be retrofitted: golangci-lint (errcheck, staticcheck, exhaustive for state/event enums, forbidigo rules banning time.Sleep in _test.go files, time.Now outside the Clock seam, and prometheus.DefaultRegisterer), go test -race on everything, govulncheck, and per-package coverage floors (internal/queue >= 90%, internal/store >= 85%) that ratchet upward only. Split CI into fast PR jobs (target <= 10 min wall) and a nightly lane placeholder. Acceptance: a deliberately added time.Sleep in a test fails CI; coverage gate fails on an uncovered queue package.

issues.title: Core primitives: ULID ids, subject matcher (+fuzz), Clock seam, sentinel errors
issues.summary: Implement the leaf packages everything else consumes: message/trace id generation with oklog/ulid/v2 (monotonic factory, defined backwards-clock behaviour, WARN on clock regression); the NATS-style subject matcher (dot tokens, * = one token, > = trailing) as a sealed pure function with a native fuzz target differential-tested against a naive reference implementation; the Clock interface seam (Now/Since/NewTimer) with real and fake implementations so all deadline logic is testable under testing/synctest; and the sentinel error set (ErrNotFound, ErrStaleAck, ErrFlowControl, ErrTooLarge, ErrShuttingDown, ...) that the API error table will map exhaustively. Acceptance: matcher fuzz runs clean for 60s in CI; ULIDs sort by time under burst generation; no package outside the seam calls time.Now (lint-enforced).

issues.title: Normative spec: SEMANTICS.md (state machine, transitions, invariants) + ADRs
issues.summary: Write docs/SEMANTICS.md as the normative specification before feature code exists: the per-(consumer,seq) state machine, the full transition table (PLAN 5.1), the invariant list I1-I11 with stable IDs, the guarantee statement, and the duplicate contract (every duplicate has a named cause). Record the adjudicated decisions as ADRs: storage engine (SQLite), protocol (HTTP/JSON), DLQ-as-stream, two durability modes, fenced tokens without HMAC, attempt counting at claim, flags+env config, cobra without viper. Conformance tests and docs/guarantees.md will cite this document by section, so it must be precise enough to implement from. Acceptance: spec merged and reviewed; every invariant has an ID that test names will reference.

issues.title: SQLite store foundation: schema v1, migrations, pragma enforcement, recovery
issues.summary: Implement internal/store on modernc.org/sqlite: the full STRICT schema v1 (meta, streams, stream_seq, messages, consumers, deliveries, events) with embedded forward-only migrations tracked in meta; the rw (MaxOpenConns=1, _txlock=immediate, WAL) and ro connection pools; a connection hook that re-asserts and reads back durability pragmas on every pooled connection and refuses to start on mismatch; data-dir flock, 0700/0600 permission checks; and the startup recovery procedure (WAL replay via open, quick_check on unclean shutdown, refuse newer schema, reclaim INFLIGHT leases to READY with jitter WITHOUT touching attempts, clean_shutdown marker). Include the //go:build cgosqlite escape-hatch file wired into a CI matrix job. Acceptance: store tests run against real files in t.TempDir() (never :memory:); a second process on the same data dir is refused; recovery of a dirty dir emits recovery.reclaimed with a correct count.

issues.title: Single-writer group-commit engine + durability modes
issues.summary: Build the writer goroutine that owns the sole rw connection: bounded cmdCh, batching up to --commit-window (2ms) / --commit-max-batch (256) into one BEGIN IMMEDIATE...COMMIT, replying to each waiter only after the commit returns, and publishing committed events to the fan-out. Implement --durability=full (synchronous=FULL) and relaxed (NORMAL, loud startup banner). Implement the fsyncgate rule: any commit error (EIO/ENOSPC) latches read-only state, logs storage.fatal at ERROR, rejects writes, and exits after a short drain — never retried. Export messq_commit_batch_size and messq_commit_duration_seconds. Acceptance: N concurrent commands produce one fsync per batch (observable via the histogram); an injected commit error latches read-only and the process refuses further writes; backpressure propagates (full cmdCh blocks handlers, never grows).

issues.title: Streams CRUD + publish path + publish dedup + peek reads
issues.summary: Implement stream create/list/info/update/delete with subject-pattern validation and per-stream limits (max_msg_size 1MiB default / 8MiB ceiling, max_msgs/bytes/age, discard old|new); the publish command through the writer (seq allocation from stream_seq, ULID id, trace_id intake from Messq-Trace-Id or W3C traceparent else minted, size enforcement); publish dedup via Messq-Msg-Id with the partial unique index (conflict returns original seq + duplicate:true + msg.dup event); batch publish as one transaction; and read-pool peek queries (by seq, by id, range with subject filter — never mutating). Acceptance: publish returns 201 only after commit; a retried publish with the same Messq-Msg-Id is idempotent; peek never touches delivery state; oversized publish gets a typed too_large error naming the limit.

issues.title: Crash harness v1: SIGKILL loop, three-valued ledger oracle, messq verify
issues.summary: Build test/crash: a harness that runs a real messq serve subprocess against a real data dir, drives publish load while maintaining an external fsynced ledger with three-valued outcomes (OK = server acked, must exist after recovery; UNKNOWN = in flight at kill, either legal; FAILED = rejected, must not exist), SIGKILLs at randomized points, restarts, and reconciles — the only correct oracle for at-least-once under crashes. Implement messq verify: the invariant checker (I1-I8 subset available at this milestone) runnable against a live daemon or a copied data dir, plus PRAGMA integrity_check plumbing, sharing its checkers with the test suite. Run a fast subset per merge and a full sweep nightly, in both durability modes (relaxed asserts no-loss under SIGKILL, loss-allowed-but-no-corruption reserved for later power-loss testing). This lands now, before the delivery engine, because the M2 exit gate (zero acknowledged loss + >=5k durable msg/s measured) decides whether the SQLite bet holds (D1 revisit trigger). Acceptance: 1000 kill cycles green; the throughput gate measured and recorded.

issues.title: Consumers: CRUD, cursor, claim/top-up, flow control
issues.summary: Implement the consumer model: create/update (idempotent)/list/info/delete with config validation (ack_wait, max_deliver default 5, backoff array, max_ack_pending default 1000, filters, start position); the cursor top-up (scan messages from cursor_seq, filter in Go with the compiled matcher, insert READY delivery rows, advance cursor past non-matches so narrow filters stay amortized O(1) per message); the claim step (attempts++, state=INFLIGHT, visible_at=now+ack_wait, committed BEFORE the fetch response per D6); and flow control (top-up refuses once pending >= max_ack_pending, emitting a rate-limited flow.blocked event). consumer info must report pending, inflight, backlog, oldest_pending age and what delivery is blocked by. Acceptance: attempts survive a crash (verified via harness); a consumer at max_ack_pending stops receiving without affecting others; filtered consumers on busy streams don't rescan history.

issues.title: Ack/nak/term/extend with fenced tokens and stale-ack detection
issues.summary: Implement the settle verbs against delivery rows: ack (DELETE the row — the terminal state IS row deletion), nak (back to READY at now + (explicit delay ?? backoff[attempt-1]) with ±20% jitter, reason stored in last_reason), term (straight to DEAD, skipping remaining attempts — the permanent-error escape), and extend (visible_at += ack_wait, capped by --max-ack-wait, attempts unchanged). Tokens are the readable fenced form stream/consumer/seq/attempt/generation validated against the live row: wrong attempt → 409 stale_ack + WARN event + metric (the double-processing race made loud); wrong generation (post-seek) → rejected; missing row → idempotent success flagged stale. Batch ack applies per-token results, never all-or-nothing. Acceptance: a late ack from a timed-out attempt is rejected while attempt N+1 is in flight; double-ack is a flagged no-op; every verb emits its event in the same transaction.

issues.title: Timeout sweeper: ack_wait expiry, backoff schedule, max_deliver
issues.summary: Implement the 250ms sweeper: one indexed UPDATE per tick flips expired INFLIGHT rows back to READY with visible_at = now + backoff[attempt-1] ± 20% jitter (emitting msg.timeout at WARN with held-for duration), and routes rows at attempts >= max_deliver to the dead path. No per-message timers, no timing wheel — an indexed visible_at column and one ticker replace all of it (250ms granularity is documented and nobody's ack-wait budget cares). The backoff array's last value repeats; max_deliver=0 means unlimited and warns at consumer creation. All timing logic is tested under testing/synctest with the fake clock (a 10-minute backoff chain tests in microseconds). Sweeper work is submitted as commands through the writer, keeping the single-writer invariant. Acceptance: a never-acked message redelivers on schedule and dead-letters after exactly max_deliver deliveries; synctest suite covers the full schedule deterministically.

issues.title: DLQ as a stream: atomic dead-lettering with provenance
issues.summary: Implement dead-lettering per D3: on DEAD with dead_policy=dlq, one transaction publishes the payload into the auto-created <stream>.dlq stream under the original subject with provenance headers (Messq-Origin-Stream/-Seq/-Consumer, Messq-Attempts, Messq-Cause max_deliver|terminated, Messq-Last-Reason, Messq-Dead-At), preserving the original msg id and trace_id so messq trace shows one continuous story; deletes the delivery row; and writes msg.dead. dead_policy=drop deletes with event only. The Messq- header prefix is reserved on publish (user headers with it are rejected with a typed error). The DLQ stream gets its own default retention (30d) and behaves like any stream for peek/sub/metrics — one mechanism, four features. Invariant I8 (DLQ conservation: each pair enters DEAD at most once, exactly one DLQ copy). Acceptance: a crash at any point never yields a dead message that is neither in the DLQ nor pending; I8 has a named passing test.

issues.title: Reference model + rapid property/invariant suite (incl. restart)
issues.summary: Build internal/model: an independent, deliberately naive (~300 line) in-memory implementation of the SEMANTICS.md transition table, written from the spec, never optimized. Drive it alongside the real broker (real SQLite file) with pgregory.net/rapid stateful testing: named actions publish/fetch/ack/nak/term/extend/advance_time/seek/purge/stale_ack/RESTART (reload the real broker from disk mid-sequence — the action that forces persistence and recovery into the property loop), with the empty-string invariant hook checking all I1-I11 plus observational equivalence after EVERY action. Failfiles are committed to testdata/regressions and replayed on every run — the regression corpus grows monotonically. Configure -rapid.checks=200 for PRs and 20000 nightly. This suite is where the real bugs are found; M3 does not exit without it green. Acceptance: 1e5 random operations across 100 seeds with zero invariant violations; a deliberately sabotaged build (ack without fence check) is caught by the suite.

issues.title: HTTP data plane: publish, long-poll fetch, settle endpoints, error envelope
issues.summary: Stand up the net/http server (Go 1.22 ServeMux method+pattern routing, no router dependency) on the Unix socket (default, 0660) and optional TCP: POST publish with raw body + Messq-* headers (201 after fsync), messages:batch, the long-poll fetch endpoint (waiter registry parked on per-consumer signal, woken by publish/redelivery-due, 200 with empty messages on timeout — one response shape), and /v1/ack|nak|term|extend with per-token results. One error envelope everywhere with the closed machine-code enum mapped exhaustively from sentinel errors (a test iterates all sentinels and fails on a missing mapping). Server hardening: MaxBytesReader before parsing, ReadHeaderTimeout, per-response write deadlines for long-poll (no global WriteTimeout), bounded --max-waiters with 503 + Retry-After. Acceptance: the five-line curl shell worker works end to end; empty fetch returns in wait_ms ± tick; a publish response is provably post-fsync (crash harness extended over HTTP).

issues.title: HTTP admin & inspection endpoints
issues.summary: Complete the control-plane surface: stream CRUD + purge (?dry_run=1), consumer CRUD + pause/resume + seek (dry-run) + pending listing (?older_than_ms), message lookup by seq and by ULID (metadata + raw-data endpoint), /v1/info (version, uptime, durability mode, db size, node id), and /healthz + /readyz with distinct meanings (readyz = recovery complete and store writable; disk pressure degrades but never flips readiness — the RabbitMQ-on-Kubernetes lesson). Inspection endpoints are strictly read-pool, never mutate delivery state, and never block the writer. PATCH endpoints validate that narrowing changes which would drop data are refused without an explicit flag. Acceptance: every endpoint in PLAN section 7 responds; peek-class endpoints verified side-effect-free by a test that diffs full store state before/after.

issues.title: AuthN/Z: bearer token file, roles, socket permissions, listener policy
issues.summary: Implement the D12 security model: Unix socket with filesystem permissions as the default ACL; TCP requires --auth-file (line-oriented: token-id, SHA-256 of a 256-bit secret, role, stream patterns) with constant-time comparison, SIGHUP reload, and three roles (publish/consume/admin) scoped per stream pattern; binding a non-loopback address without auth is a fatal startup error. Token secrets implement slog.LogValuer so they are structurally unloggable; only the short token id appears in logs and in the actor field of admin events. auth.denied events + messq_auth_denied_total metric. A generated route-registry test asserts every mutating route declares its required role — an endpoint without an authz entry fails the build (the one idea worth taking from plan 08 at this tax bracket). Acceptance: permission matrix test over (role x route) passes; canary secret never appears in any captured log output.

issues.title: Daemon lifecycle: signals, graceful drain, SIGHUP reload, systemd unit
issues.summary: Implement the lifecycle state machine: SIGTERM → stop accepting → release parked long-polls cleanly → drain in-flight handlers (--drain-timeout 10s) → final commit → wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE) → clean_shutdown marker → exit 0; SIGHUP → reload log level and auth tokens with a logged diff; sd_notify READY only after recovery completes, STOPPING on drain, with Type=notify. Drain is an optimization, never a correctness requirement — kill -9 remains safe and the crash suite asserts it. Ship the hardened systemd unit (User=messq, StateDirectory, ProtectSystem=strict, NoNewPrivileges, RestrictAddressFamilies, empty CapabilityBoundingSet, LimitNOFILE, Restart=on-failure with StartLimitBurst so a dying disk doesn't grind evidence away). Acceptance: systemctl restart messq mid-load loses nothing and logs recovery.reclaimed; systemd-analyze security score recorded.

issues.title: API contract tests + executable curl golden tests
issues.summary: Lock the wire as a contract: httptest-based coverage of every endpoint's success shape and every documented error code (the closed enum from PLAN section 7); JSON response shapes validated against committed schemas so removing/retyping a field fails the build with a message demanding a version bump; and the executable-documentation harness — every curl transcript in README/PROTOCOL docs is extracted and run against a fresh daemon with normalized golden output (ULIDs/timestamps masked). Add the auth-denial and listener-policy cases (non-loopback plaintext bind fails at startup). This issue also establishes the docs-cannot-rot infrastructure reused by the CLI testscript suite later. Acceptance: the five-line shell worker in the README is a passing CI test; a renamed JSON field fails CI.

issues.title: Event pipeline: vocabulary, in-transaction events table, slog handlers, sampling
issues.summary: Wire the observability spine per D11: the closed event vocabulary (PLAN 9.2) emitted from a single applyTransition-style choke point so it is structurally impossible to change state without its event; event rows written in the same transaction as the state change (zero extra fsyncs, audit cannot lie); the event fan-out goroutine feeding slog + metrics + followers from committed events only. Implement both slog handlers — JSON (slog.NewJSONHandler with ReplaceAttr enforcing the frozen field schema and payload redaction) and the ~180-line human console handler validated with testing/slogtest — plus slog.LevelVar with SIGHUP, per-message sampling (hash(trace_id)%N so a sampled message logs its whole lifecycle), the never-sampleable allow-list for problem events, and --trace-subjects targeted verbosity. Event-table retention knobs (--event-retention 72h, --event-max-rows) enforced by the janitor. Golden log tests pin event names and field sets. Acceptance: a scripted publish→timeout→nak→ack scenario produces the exact golden event sequence on all three surfaces; payload canary never appears in logs.

issues.title: messq trace + events query/follow API
issues.summary: Ship the flagship: GET /v1/messages/{id}/trace and GET /v1/events with filters (msg_id, trace_id, stream, consumer, event, since, limit) plus follow=1 streaming NDJSON for live tailing (bounded ring per follower; overflow drops with a loud lost-events marker, never blocking the data path). The messq trace renderer produces the timeline from PLAN section 8 — relative offsets, attempt/of, causes, reasons, the ack.stale line, the duplicates-accounted-for summary, and next-command hints (dlq show / redrive / peek --raw); --trace-id shows every message sharing a trace as one story across DLQ hops and redrives. Output is golden-tested byte-for-byte (this screenshot is the product). Acceptance: trace of a message that timed out, was naked, went to DLQ and was redriven reads as one continuous history; messq events --follow shows live transitions.

issues.title: Prometheus metrics, shipped alert rules, Grafana dashboard
issues.summary: Implement the full metric set from PLAN 9.4 on a custom prometheus.NewRegistry (promauto.With, promhttp.HandlerFor with MaxRequestsInFlight): counters from the event fan-out, latency/commit histograms, and backlog/pending/oldest-pending-age/dlq-depth gauges computed by a custom Collector querying SQLite at scrape time with a 5s cache (recomputed-from-truth gauges cannot drift). Enforce the cardinality rule with a test: labels are stream and consumer only, never subject or ids. Ship contrib/prometheus/alerts.yml (DLQ growth, oldest_pending_age > 15m, stale-ack rate, retention.blocked, disk ETA) and contrib/grafana/messq.json (one screen: alive / working / suffering / losing). Metric names + label sets are golden-tested via prometheus/testutil. Acceptance: golden exposition test green; a subject-labelled metric fails CI; dashboard renders against a bench run.

issues.title: Go client package (pkg/client) + Worker helper
issues.summary: Build the thin Go client the CLI itself will consume (D14 — the CLI using it guarantees it is real): Client with Publish/Fetch/Ack/Nak/Term/Extend plus stream/consumer admin calls, taking an *http.Client so callers own transports and timeouts, unix:// and http(s):// addresses. Add the Worker helper: Consume(ctx, stream, consumer, handler) implementing the fetch/heartbeat/settle loop with automatic Extend at ack_wait/2 while the handler runs (killing the #1 at-least-once footgun in the library, not in every user's code), nil→ack, ErrPermanent→term, error→nak, panic→nak+logged; reconnect with jittered backoff; bounded batch publish. No codegen, no exposed wire structs beyond stable types; < ~800 LOC. Acceptance: a Worker survives a daemon restart mid-batch with zero lost work and zero stale-ack surprises; client is exercised by every subsequent CLI test.

issues.title: CLI framework: cobra root, output contract, exit codes
issues.summary: Establish the CLI chassis every command inherits: cobra root with RunE, SilenceUsage/SilenceErrors, persistent --addr/--output/--token-file/--timeout flags and MESSQ_* env fallback (three-layer precedence, ~100 lines, no viper); the output renderer (table on TTY with aligned columns, relative times, abbreviated ULIDs and NO_COLOR handling; json/ndjson otherwise — never a third mode; data to stdout, narration to stderr); the teaching-error type (what happened / why / next commands / help topic) rendered from server error envelopes without inventing text; and the documented exit-code contract (0 ok, 1 error, 2 usage, 3 not found, 4 conflict/stale, 5 empty/timeout, 6 unreachable, 7 permission). A DX linter test walks the command tree failing any command without Long+Example. Acceptance: exit codes verified by tests; human and JSON faces both golden-testable.

issues.title: CLI core commands: stream/consumer/pub/sub/peek/pending/lag/ack-family
issues.summary: Implement the working command surface: stream add/ls/info/edit/rm/purge and consumer add/ls/info/edit/rm/pause/resume (noun-verb); the hot-path verbs one word deep — pub (stdin/file/args, headers, --msg-id, --count), sub (print + auto-ack, --manual), peek (--seq/--last/--subject/--raw), pending (--older-than, sorted by deadline), lag (the incident-overview table with attention markers and next-command footers); and manual transitions ack/nak/term/extend by token for symmetry with the daemon (anything the daemon can do to a message, a human can do by hand). consumer add prints the computed retry horizon from the backoff schedule and warns on footguns (max_deliver=0, backoff shorter than max_deliver). Acceptance: the lag table matches the PLAN section 8 shape; every list command supports all three output modes; every inspect command ends with the next useful command.

issues.title: messq sub --exec: shell-script workers with the sysexits contract
issues.summary: Implement the widest-funnel feature: messq sub <stream> <consumer> --exec CMD [--concurrency N] runs the command per message with the payload on stdin and metadata in MESSQ_* env vars (MSG_ID, SEQ, SUBJECT, ATTEMPT, MAX_DELIVER, TRACE_ID, DEADLINE, HEADER_*, plus a traceparent). Exit code is the ack: 0→ack, 75 (EX_TEMPFAIL)→nak with the consumer's backoff, 65 (EX_DATAERR)→term straight to DLQ, other non-zero→nak, killed-by-signal→nak with the signal as reason. The child's stderr (first 4 KiB) becomes the nak reason, visible in trace and the DLQ — the reason a job failed is visible from the queue, not only the worker's logs. Automatic extend heartbeat at ack_wait/2 while the child runs, bounded by --exec-timeout. First failure prints a one-time hint explaining the exit-code mapping. Acceptance: a bash one-liner is a durable retrying dead-lettering worker; concurrency respects max_ack_pending; testscript covers ack/nak/term/signal paths.

issues.title: Quickstart, shell completions, help topics, testscript golden suite
issues.summary: Finish the first-five-minutes experience: messq quickstart (guided tour on a throwaway data dir — publish, ack, nak, a deliberate timeout-to-DLQ, ending with an unprompted messq trace of the dead message and the redrive command; it is the demo, and it is a testscript test so it can never rot); messq serve --dev (ephemeral dir, human logs, auto-create streams); dynamic shell completions for bash/zsh/fish completing live stream/consumer names via the Unix socket with a 200ms budget and silent failure; help topics (concepts, lifecycle, durability, exit-codes, scripting); man pages via cobra doc generation. Establish the full testscript (.txtar) golden suite covering every command's human and JSON faces with a fake-clock env, wired into CI with an -update flow. Acceptance: cold machine to completed quickstart in under 60 seconds; every README command block executes in CI.

issues.title: Retention (limits/workqueue), housekeeping, disk safety
issues.summary: Implement the janitor's full job: retention=limits (age/count/bytes, oldest first, discard=old|new — new rejects publishes with a typed error instead of deleting) with the safety rule that a message holding an outstanding delivery row is never silently deleted (retention.blocked event + metric + shipped alert names the guilty consumer); retention=workqueue (delete once all consumers passed and no delivery rows remain, in the 60s sweep so acks stay cheap); dedup-key expiry; event-table trim; WAL checkpoint (TRUNCATE) above --wal-max-bytes; incremental vacuum on freelist growth; stream purge with dry-run. Disk safety: --min-free-bytes (256 MiB default) below which publishes are rejected while acks/naks/DLQ writes continue (a full disk must never wedge the ack path), disk state in /healthz detail and metrics, readiness never coupled to disk pressure. Acceptance: a week-long simulated workload holds the file size bounded; the ENOSPC scenario drains and recovers without restart or corruption (full loopback-fs test lands in seq 32).

issues.title: Seek + replay + destructive-action discipline
issues.summary: Implement the two distinct recovery tools and the safety rails around all destructive verbs. Seek: move one consumer's cursor (start/new/seq:N/time:T via the published_at index), bumping generation so all outstanding tokens fence, optionally dropping pending rows, with an exact impact preview. Replay: re-publish copies of a seq/time range (new seq, new id, Messq-Replay-Of header, original trace_id preserved, optional subject filter and target stream) — the reprocess-yesterday button. Discipline applied uniformly to seek/replay/purge/rm (and inherited by dlq redrive in seq 29): --dry-run renders the exact preview through the same renderer as the real run, confirmation is by typing the resource name (never y/n), non-TTY requires --yes, and every execution writes an admin.action event with actor, params and before/after counts. Acceptance: seek --dry-run counts match the real run exactly; replayed messages trace back to their origin; a purge without --confirm <name> is refused.

issues.title: DLQ operations: ls/show/redrive with guard rails
issues.summary: Ship the DLQ triage workflow with the war-story guard rails baked in: messq dlq ls (grouped by cause/subject, showing growth rate next to depth — 400 in five minutes is an incident, 400 last Tuesday is a chore), dlq show <id> (full record, headers, last error, link to trace), dlq purge, and dlq redrive — rate-limited by default (--rate 10/s), --limit defaults to 100 with no replay-everything flag, republishes with Messq-Redrive-Of and Messq-Redrive-Count headers, and refuses a message already redriven 3 times without --force (the re-DLQ loop is how a redrive becomes a second incident). stream info warns when a DLQ has no consumer (an unread DLQ is a silent data sink). All redrive actions are dry-runnable, name-confirmed and audited per seq 28. Acceptance: redrive of a still-failing message re-dead-letters and the trace shows the full loop; guard-rail refusals have teaching errors.

issues.title: Backup/restore (VACUUM INTO) + messq doctor
issues.summary: Implement messq backup <path> as VACUUM INTO on the read pool — a consistent online snapshot with no downtime, verified by opening and quick_check before returning 0; restore is documented as stop/copy/start and messq status reports restored-from so a missing tail is never a mystery. Implement messq doctor, the diagnostic that encodes operational knowledge as prose findings with exact fix commands: verifies live durability pragmas ('a 201 survives power loss: YES'), measures actual fdatasync latency on the data dir and warns on implausibly fast syncs (lying write cache), flags ack_wait below observed ack p99, max_deliver=0 without DLQ, DLQs growing with no drain, consumers idle for days, tiny consumer-less streams (typo detection), disk headroom vs retention, and relaxed durability. Exit code reflects findings for cron use. Acceptance: doctor detects each seeded misconfiguration in a fixture daemon; backup taken under load restores to a verify-clean data dir.

issues.title: messq bench + honest performance methodology and numbers
issues.summary: Ship the load generator in the binary so anyone can reproduce our numbers on their hardware: messq bench publish|e2e|replay with --publishers/--consumers/--size/--rate/--duration, open-loop by default with coordinated-omission-corrected latency (requests scheduled, latency measured from intended dispatch time; a saturated generator invalidates the run rather than lying), percentiles from histograms, and a --kill-every mode that SIGKILLs and restarts the daemon mid-run reporting lost=0 duplicates=N — operators can run the durability claim themselves. Every emitted report includes rate, size, connections, durability mode, kernel, filesystem, device and commit. Wire a nightly benchstat comparison against the stored baseline (regression opens an issue; not a merge gate — noise-gated merges train people to ignore gates). Publish docs/benchmarks.md with the measured M2-gate numbers and methodology. Acceptance: bench e2e reproduces the PLAN section 12 targets on the reference box; the docs page states hardware and mode next to every number.

issues.title: Fault-injection points + crash matrix + ENOSPC/EIO/clock scenarios
issues.summary: Extend the crash harness into the full hardening matrix. Add named fault points behind a messq_fault build tag with an env-driven activation grammar (percent/count/action — the failpoint idea without the codegen): before/after commit, after-commit-before-reply, during checkpoint, during dead-letter, during recovery. Run the kill sweep across fault points x durability modes nightly. Add the resource-exhaustion scenarios on real filesystems: a small loopback ext4 filled to ENOSPC (must reject publishes with the typed error, keep consuming/acking, recover without restart, no corruption), injected EIO on commit (must latch read-only, never continue — a test asserts the daemon cannot keep writing after a failed sync), clock jumps ±1h (monotonic deadlines unaffected; mass-timeout jitter verified), client disconnect mid-fetch and never-acking consumers (flow control holds, leases expire, ack.stale observed). Acceptance: all scenarios have named green CI jobs; the harness catches a deliberately introduced synchronous=OFF sabotage build.

issues.title: Fuzzing corpus + nightly jobs + soak test
issues.summary: Complete the fuzz surface: subject matcher (already seeded in seq 3 — extend corpus), ack-token parser (no input panics; no forged token validates), JSON request decoders, header parsing, and the command-sequence fuzzer that decodes fuzz bytes into core commands applied against the state machine with invariants checked after each step (an unguided model checker — historically the cheapest state-machine bug finder). 60s per target on PRs, 30 min nightly, all crashers committed to the corpus permanently. Stand up the nightly soak: 1h+ (weekly longer) at load with 10% naks, seeded poison messages, consumer kills, broker SIGKILL every 5 minutes, retention active; final assertions are conservation (published = acked + termed + dead + expired + still_pending), flat RSS, flat goroutine count, verify clean, and DLQ contents exactly the injected poison set. Acceptance: all fuzz targets clean; two consecutive green soak nights before the v1.0 tag.

issues.title: Upgrade fixtures + schema-version gate tests
issues.summary: Make on-disk compatibility a tested promise before it is frozen at 1.0: commit golden data-directory fixtures (testdata/datadirs/) containing non-trivial state — pending messages, a populated DLQ, a mid-backoff message, a post-seek consumer with a bumped generation — produced by the current schema and by each future released version. Tests assert the current binary opens each fixture, migrates forward inside one transaction, passes verify --deep, and continues delivering correctly; a fixture with a NEWER schema version is refused with exact instructions (never auto-guess, never partially parse); downgrade at equal schema version works. Document the upgrade procedure (check format version, backup, upgrade, verify) in the ops docs. This is the most commonly skipped test category and the most expensive to skip. Acceptance: the fixture suite runs on every merge; the v1 schema is frozen at the 1.0 tag with this suite as its guard.

issues.title: 1.0 documentation set: README, guarantees, operations, runbooks, comparisons
issues.summary: Write the documentation that is itself a trust artifact: the final README (two sentences, the messq trace output block, the three-command quickstart, 'When NOT to use messq', comparison table, install — its only job is making the reader run quickstart); docs/guarantees.md where every row names an invariant ID and the CI job that proves it (a guarantee without both gets deleted); docs/OPERATIONS.md with the top runbooks (consumer stuck, DLQ filling, disk filling, torn tail after crash, duplicate deliveries explained, ack_wait tuning, accidental purge) each with executable confirm/mitigate command blocks; PROTOCOL.md and the log-field schema as versioned contracts; fair comparison pages (vs JetStream / Redis Streams / Postgres jobs table / Kafka, each ending 'choose them if...'); docs/non-goals.md; and graduating-to-jetstream.md (the anti-lock-in page). The incident-shaped tutorial ('A message went missing. Find it.') is the signature doc. All command blocks execute in CI via the seq 18/26 harness. Acceptance: docs build; every fenced command runs; guarantees table cross-references pass.

issues.title: Packaging & release engineering + v1.0.0 tag
issues.summary: Ship the distribution path: goreleaser producing reproducible static linux/amd64+arm64 binaries (CGO_ENABLED=0, -trimpath, mod_timestamp), .deb/.rpm via nfpm containing the binary, hardened systemd unit, messq system user, completions and man pages in the right paths; a scratch-based container image; checksums and cosign-signed release artifacts; an install.sh; SBOM. Wire the release workflow to run the full gate suite. Then grind the v1.0 release-gate checklist to zero — every invariant has a named passing test, crash matrix green in both durability modes, soak clean, upgrade fixtures green, docs command blocks green, benchmarks published — and tag v1.0.0 with the written compatibility promise (HTTP API shapes, CLI --json shapes, log schema, on-disk format, error codes). Acceptance: apt install messq && systemctl start messq on a clean VM, then the quickstart, with no other steps; messq version --json reports the frozen format version.

issues.title: Phase 2: delayed delivery (Messq-Deliver-At)
issues.summary: Add scheduled publishing: a Messq-Deliver-At (absolute) or Messq-Delay (relative) header on publish makes the message invisible to all consumers until the given time — implemented on the existing visible_at machinery (the delivery row is created READY with a future visible_at at top-up time), so no new storage or timer subsystem is required. Scheduled time is visible in peek, trace and consumer info; delayed messages are counted separately from backlog so lag alerts don't fire on intentional scheduling. New invariant I12-a: no message is delivered before its deliver-at time, across restarts and clock jumps (deadline arithmetic stays monotonic-clock based; a wall-clock jump is logged and cannot deliver early). Ships with a new simulator/property action, events, metrics, CLI flag (messq pub --at/--after) and docs, per the phase-2 rule. Acceptance: 1e5 scheduled messages land within one sweeper tick of their time in synctest; restart preserves schedules.

issues.title: Phase 2: ordered-by-subject consumers
issues.summary: Implement ordered=subject on a consumer: at most one message per subject may be unresolved (READY-claimed or INFLIGHT) at a time, and the claim always selects the lowest outstanding seq per subject — so a naked message waiting out its backoff blocks later messages on the same subject, which is what 'ordered' must mean. Head-of-line blocking is displayed, never hidden: consumer info lists blocked subjects with the blocking message, attempt and next-retry time, and a hol_blocked metric exists. Document the poison interaction honestly (a poison message stalls its subject until max_deliver exhausts to the DLQ, unblocking the subject; note the ordering gap this creates and the term escape hatch). Default remains none. New invariant I13-a (at most one unresolved per subject per ordered consumer, claims in per-subject seq order) checked by the model suite with a new ordered dimension in the generator; sub --exec caps concurrency per subject. Acceptance: property suite green with ordering enabled; blocked-subject display matches reality under a seeded poison message.

issues.title: Phase 2: per-consumer delivery rate limiting
issues.summary: Add --max-rate N/s on a consumer: a token bucket consulted at claim time that strictly narrows the fetch guard, so it cannot break any invariant by construction. The single most requested feature after a DLQ redrive goes badly — it lets an operator drain a large backlog into a fragile downstream at a controlled pace, and pairs with dlq redrive --rate for the same reason. Rate-limited state is visible: consumer info shows delivery_blocked_by=rate_limit, fetch returns the empty batch with a typed hold reason, and a messq_flow_control_engaged metric accrues. Configurable live via consumer edit without restart. New invariant: deliveries in any window <= rate + burst, checked in synctest. Acceptance: a backlogged consumer with --max-rate 10/s receives 10±1 msg/s while others are unaffected; disabling the limit resumes full speed immediately.

issues.title: Phase 2: native TLS listener with hot certificate reload
issues.summary: Add first-party TLS for deployments that cannot front a reverse proxy: --tls-cert/--tls-key on the TCP listener using stdlib crypto/tls (MinVersion 1.2, TLS 1.3 preferred), GetCertificate-based hot reload on SIGHUP so rotation needs no restart, and optional mTLS via --tls-client-ca with the client identity (SAN/CN) becoming the principal recorded in auth events. Listener policy tightens: with TLS available, plaintext non-loopback remains a fatal error with a message pointing at either TLS flags or proxy-into-unix-socket. Conformance tests: reject TLS < 1.2, reject missing client cert when mTLS is required, reject a cert from the wrong CA, and verify identity checks live in VerifyConnection so session resumption cannot bypass them. Docs update the deployment matrix. Acceptance: TLS conformance suite green; cert rotation under load drops zero requests.

issues.title: Phase 2: worker attribution & per-worker caps (consumer groups, lite)
issues.summary: Multiple workers sharing one consumer already works correctly because acks are fenced (D7); this issue adds the visibility and safety around it rather than a Kafka-style group protocol — explicitly no partition assignment, no rebalance barrier, no member leases beyond the ack deadline (the ack deadline IS the lease). Fetch accepts a worker identity (client name/host/pid); deliveries record it; pending/inflight listings and trace lines show which worker holds each message; messq workers lists members with last-seen and in-flight counts; per-worker in-flight caps subdivide max_ack_pending; per-worker metric labels are bounded by registered workers. A dead worker's messages simply ack-wait out and redeliver elsewhere — already-tested machinery. New invariant: a seq is INFLIGHT to at most one worker at a time. Acceptance: kill 1 of 3 workers mid-batch — only its in-flight set redelivers, within ack_wait, attributed correctly in trace.

issues.title: Phase 2: audit export (events NDJSON export & sink)
issues.summary: Serve the compliance/archival ICP: messq events export --since/--until/--stream --gzip streams the events table as NDJSON with the frozen log-field schema (so an auditor or a SIEM ingests it without custom tooling), plus an optional --audit-sink path on the daemon that appends terminal and admin events to a rotated NDJSON file continuously for retention beyond the in-database window. Export is a pure read path (read pool, chunked, resumable via since-id), so it is trivially safe and cannot affect the write path. Document the retention interplay (export-then-shrink guidance that doctor already suggests when the events table dominates the DB) and the restore/replay story for exported archives. New invariant: an exported stream folds to the same state as the live events table over the same range (I10 applied to the export). Acceptance: a 10M-row export round-trips through the fold check; the sink survives rotation under load without dropping terminal events.
